design: Single-table design: every entity lives in one table with a composite key (PK = partition key, SK = sort key). The optional GSI1 (GSI1PK, GSI1SK) gives a second access path. Create the table with: aws dynamodb create-table --cli-input-json file://database/dynamodb_schema.json
capacity: PAY_PER_REQUEST (On-Demand), as the AWS Learner Lab rules ask

indexing_policy.primary_key: PK + SK: direct GetItem/PutItem/UpdateItem of one entity, never a scan for single reads
indexing_policy.GSI1: sparse index: only items that have GSI1PK are in it (users and products). Users by email (sign-in, unique email) and products by category sorted by price. Projection ALL so a query never needs a second read.
indexing_policy.not_indexed_on_purpose: carts, favorites and stock reservations are always read by their own key (PK = owner or order), so they have no GSI attributes and cost nothing in the index

attributes.name: string
attributes.password_hash: Argon2id hash (older accounts: scrypt, upgraded on their next sign-in); never the password

attributes.name: string
attributes.image_url: optional string: photo in the S3 bucket

entities.written_by: Lambda routes /productos/* (ProductServiceImplementation); 17,000 items loaded with BatchWriteItem by scripts/load_to_dynamo.py

attributes.lines: list (max 30) of {line_id (12 hex), product_id, size, color, qty 1..10}

attributes.items: map product_id -> units taken from stock

entities.written_by: atomic TransactWriteItems of /productos/reservar (with the stock discount) and /productos/liberar (with the restock)

access_patterns.need: products of a category sorted by price
load the whole catalog at app start
access_patterns.operation: Scan with filter begins_with(PK, 'PRODUCT#') AND SK = 'METADATA', pages of 1,000

related_relational_data.MySQL finance_db: orders.buyer_id -> USER.id_user; order_items.product_id -> PRODUCT.product_id; orders.order_id -> STOCK_RESERVATION.order_id
related_relational_data.PostgreSQL: categories.category_id -> PRODUCT.category_id; sellers.seller_id -> PRODUCT.seller_id; sellers.user_id -> USER.id_user; reviews/analytics/alerts.product_id -> PRODUCT.product_id
